notes:
Two tablets no longer hand out the same piston number.

**Place a general 5 on one tablet and the other will offer 6, not 5 again.** In 2.03 and 2.04 the "carry on from the last one you placed" counter lived only on the tablet you placed from, so each tablet counted on its own and they could collide. The rule it replaced read the numbers already on the page, which is why both tablets used to agree without being told anything.

Now the counter decides where to start and **the pistons already on the page decide what is unavailable**: it takes the next number after the one you placed, then steps past anything already used on that layer and memory level. All of the behaviour from the last two updates is unchanged — place 12 and get 13, delete 13 and get 13 back, renumber 320 down to 250 and get 251 — and a number the other tablet has taken is now skipped instead of duplicated.

A number on one memory level does not block the same number on another.
